name: Pacific Edge Limited
overview: Pacific Edge Limited is a Dunedin, New Zealand-headquartered molecular diagnostics company that develops and commercializes the Cxbladder suite of urine-based RNA/DNA biomarker tests for bladder cancer detection, risk stratification (hematuria evaluation) and post-treatment surveillance. The company operates CLIA/CAP-certified laboratories in New Zealand and the US and is dual-listed on the NZX and ASX (ticker PEB). Pacific Edge's business has been dominated for the past two years by the loss and attempted recovery of US Medicare reimbursement, which historically represented roughly 60% of company revenue.

business_model.summary: Pacific Edge sells laboratory-developed diagnostic tests (Cxbladder Triage, Detect, Monitor, and next-generation Triage Plus/Surveillance Plus) that clinicians order per-patient; revenue is transactional (fee-per-test) rather than recurring/subscription, driven by test volumes and reimbursement rates (Medicare, Medicare Advantage, commercial insurance, and NZ/APAC public and private payers). The company is not yet profitable and depends on US commercial scale-up and reimbursement policy to reach breakeven.

revenue_streams.name: US (Americas) Cxbladder testing
revenue_streams.trend: declining post Medicare non-coverage, expected to recover on LCD finalization

revenue_streams.name: New Zealand / APAC (Rest of World) Cxbladder testing

business_model.customer_type: B2B2C - tests ordered by urologists/primary care physicians (clinician-directed), reimbursed by government payers (Medicare/Te Whatu Ora), Medicare Advantage, and private/commercial health insurers; patients themselves also bear enhanced patient-responsibility charges for non-covered tests
business_model.geographic_mix: FY26: Americas (US) ~83% of operating revenue (down from 91% in FY25 due to Medicare non-coverage), Rest of World (primarily New Zealand, with developing Australia/Southeast Asia) ~17%; NZ is the mature, market-dominant home base with ~70% public healthcare coverage reach

main_competitors: UroSEEK and other emerging urinary biomarker/liquid biopsy entrants
competitive_position.market_position: First-mover and clinical-evidence leader in urine-based molecular biomarker testing for bladder cancer; market-dominant position in New Zealand (~70% public healthcare coverage reach); in the US it is a small-scale, single-product-family diagnostics company whose commercial position is currently constrained almost entirely by the Medicare non-coverage determination rather than by competitive displacement

moat_factors.description: Pacific Edge has built the most extensive analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility evidence base of any urine biomarker for bladder cancer, including the STRATA RCT, DRIVE study, and a multi-year roadmap of further trials (AUSSIE, microDRIVE, LOBSTER, CREDIBLE, OCTOPUS); management and independent reviewers (ECRI, Avalon Healthcare) state no competing product has matched this AV/CV/CU evidence framework

Cxbladder Triage is the only biomarker with 'Grade A' evidence included in the American Urological Association's Microhematuria Guideline (amended Feb 2025), which is the key clinical and policy lever driving both physician adoption and the Medicare coverage reconsideration

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory/coverage barrier to entry (draft LCD exclusivity)
moat_factors.description: The May 2026 draft Novitas LCD (DL40378) names only Cxbladder Triage and Triage Plus as reimbursable for hematuria evaluation, explicitly excluding competing biomarkers due to insufficient evidence - if finalized this creates a de facto reimbursement moat
Wholly owned, accredited laboratories in NZ and US provide quality control and margin capture versus a kit-distribution model, though this also concentrates operational/key-person risk

Deep roster of US urology key opinion leaders (UT Southwestern, Vanderbilt, NYU Langone, Fred Hutchinson, etc.) serving as consultants, clinical advisory board members and trial investigators supports credibility and guideline influence

weaknesses: Extreme customer/payer concentration risk - a single Medicare Administrative Contractor (Novitas) decision devastated ~60% of revenue for over a year and remains the single largest swing factor for the stock
Small scale relative to well-capitalized diagnostics/oncology peers who could out-invest in evidence generation or competing biomarkers
US sales force has been cut drastically (from >30 FTE to ~8-12 FTE) to conserve cash, constraining near-term volume recovery even if coverage returns
Single core product franchise (urine-based bladder cancer biomarkers) with no other disease-area diversification
International (ex-US, ex-NZ) expansion depends on a still-unlaunched kitted IVD product, currently paused for capital preservation

growth_drivers: Finalization of the draft Novitas LCD (DL40378), expected by end of calendar 2026, which would restore Medicare coverage for Cxbladder Triage and newly cover Triage Plus at a 75% higher price (US$1,328 vs US$760)
Migration of the US test mix from legacy Detect/Triage to higher-priced, higher-performance Triage Plus, improving average selling price and unit economics
Growing commercial payer coverage wins (Blue Cross Blue Shield NC/SC/Kansas City, Highmark, Sentara, Kaiser Permanente EMR integration) reducing reliance on Medicare alone
Development of Cxbladder Surveillance Plus (ddPCR-based NMIBC surveillance test) targeting a crosswalk price of US$1,800, with CPT-PLA coding submission targeted December 2026
International expansion via a kitted IVD (Triage Plus IVD) enabling decentralized deployment through accredited lab partners in Europe, Australia and Southeast Asia (currently paused pending capital)
New Zealand national hematuria evaluation pathway under consideration by Te Whatu Ora (Health NZ) for FY27
APAC volume growth (Singapore General Hospital, Townsville University Hospital) with APAC operations nearing regional profitability

Structurally favorable secular trend: declining US urologist workforce per capita (23.8/100k trending toward 15.8/100k by 2035) increasing the value of a non-invasive triage tool that reduces cystoscopy burden

business.description: The draft LCD is not yet final; if Novitas does not finalize coverage for Triage/Triage Plus, or delays significantly, the company says it would need a significant restructuring and likely further capital raising, with a material adverse impact on financial performance and viability
Sales FTEs cut to ~8-12 from 30+ to conserve cash; rebuilding commercial reach to capture a coverage win will take time and investment
Reliance on lab operations, third-party component suppliers and IT/digital systems; any reliability, accuracy or cyber-security failure could damage reputation and results delivery
Large, well-funded oncology diagnostics companies could develop or acquire competing urine biomarker technology, though none currently match Cxbladder's AV/CV/CU evidence base
Triage Plus IVD and Surveillance Plus development could be delayed, more expensive than expected, or ultimately unsuccessful, especially given re-phasing/pausing of R&D to conserve capital

financial.description: FY26 net loss after tax of $35.8m (up from $29.9m in FY25) against cash, equivalents and short-term deposits of only $7.8m at 31 March 2026; management states the May-June 2026 $36.1m capital raise provides 'over 12 months' cash runway based on FY26 cash burn rates, but that runway is explicitly conditioned on Medicare re-coverage progress

Multiple raises in the last 12 months (August 2025: ~$20.7m; May 2026: $25.4m placement; June 2026: $10.7m retail offer, together $36.1m) at depressed prices (as low as NZ$0.17/share) have materially diluted existing shareholders and are likely to recur if coverage timelines slip further
US-dollar denominated Medicare/commercial revenue and costs versus NZD reporting currency and NZD/AUD dual listing create translation and economic FX exposure

regulatory.description: Novitas (the Medicare Administrative Contractor) retains full discretion over the timing and final content of the LCD; the draft published 14 May 2026 is subject to a comment period and could be narrowed, delayed, or withdrawn before finalization, expected around end of CY2026 to Q2 CY2027
Continued AUA guideline inclusion (and future guideline revisions expected 2027) materially affects both clinical adoption and payer policy; loss of guideline status would be damaging
Must maintain CLIA, CAP, ISO13485, ISO15189, IVDR (EU) and other certifications across NZ and US labs; audit failures could disrupt operations or market access

macro.risk: US healthcare policy and reimbursement environment
macro.description: Broader shifts in CMS/Medicare policy, government shutdown or budget dynamics, or MAC contractor changes could affect the pace and outcome of coverage decisions independent of Cxbladder's own evidence

A prolonged economic downturn could reduce or reprioritize healthcare spending in the US, NZ or Southeast Asia; geopolitical instability, tariffs and supply chain disruption are also flagged as risks by the company

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global bladder cancer diagnostics/molecular oncology testing market is expanding, driven by an aging population, rising hematuria referral volumes, and growing acceptance of non-invasive biomarker alternatives to cystoscopy; management estimates a US$10.8bn global addressable market at Medicare-approved pricing for Triage Plus/Surveillance Plus across US, APAC and other markets
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low direct cyclicality (diagnostic testing driven by disease incidence, not discretionary spend), but company-specific 'cyclicality' is currently dominated by a binary regulatory/reimbursement catalyst (Medicare LCD) rather than the macro economy
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High indirectly - as an unprofitable, cash-burning growth company reliant on repeated equity capital raises, higher rates and risk-off small-cap sentiment increase the cost and dilution of raising capital
key_input_costs: Laboratory reagents/consumables and test-kit components (including EU-based urine sampling system supplier)
Legal/regulatory costs (elevated in FY26 due to Medicare coverage litigation/appeals)

recent_developments.event: Annual Shareholders' Meeting held 20 August 2026 in Auckland; shareholders approved governance resolutions and ratified the May/June 2026 capital raisings; Simon Flood's first AGM as Chair

Q1 FY27 investor update: US commercial test volumes dipped 2.4% q/q to 3,295 (reflecting further sales-force reduction ahead of the draft LCD release), while APAC commercial tests rose 12.9% to 1,158; company continued claim-by-claim Medicare billing under the draft LCD framework
Board approved a further $10.7 million retail share offer (approved 2 June 2026), completing the $36.1 million total capital raise alongside the May placement

Novitas published draft Local Coverage Determination 'Urine-based Biomarkers in Patients with Microhematuria' (DL40378) on 14 May 2026, proposing Medicare coverage explicitly for Cxbladder Triage and Triage Plus (and no competing biomarkers), with Triage Plus priced at US$1,328/test (75% above the prior US$760 Triage/Detect price); Pacific Edge immediately raised $25.4 million via placement and began claim-by-claim billing under the draft policy

FY2026 annual results (year ended 31 March 2026) reported: operating revenue $11.5m (down 47.4% YoY), total revenue $13.6m, net loss after tax $35.8m (up from $29.9m in FY25), cash/equivalents/short-term deposits of $7.8m at year end, total laboratory throughput down 16.3% to 24,190 tests

Novitas convened an expert Contractor Advisory Committee (CAC) meeting (19 February 2026) to gather clinical opinion on urine-based biomarkers for microhematuria; panelists expressed strong support for Cxbladder, directly precipitating the subsequent draft LCD

H1 FY2026 results (six months to 30 September 2025): operating revenue $5.9m (down 45.8% YoY), net loss after tax $19.1m, cash/short-term deposits $22.1m; management flagged it was 'considering capital initiatives' due to a longer-than-expected Medicare re-coverage timeline

DRIVE Study (Savage et al.) published in Journal of Urologic Oncology, providing pivotal clinical validation of Cxbladder Triage Plus across both microhematuria and gross hematuria patients, submitted to Novitas and the AUA to support coverage and guideline consideration
Pacific Edge raised approximately $20.7 million in new equity to fund continued US market presence and the Medicare reconsideration/appeals process

Medicare non-coverage of Cxbladder Triage, Detect, Monitor and Triage Plus became formally effective (24 April 2025) following the earlier LCD withdrawal, eliminating the majority of US Medicare revenue and precipitating the reconsideration requests and new LCD request that ultimately led to the May 2026 draft LCD

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Simon Flood: 'Pacific Edge finished the year in a materially stronger strategic position than it entered it... we are looking forward to seeing this support rewarded with a return to growth.' CEO Dr Peter Meintjes: 'FY26 was an unequivocal validation of our strategy that puts generation of clinical evidence at the heart of value creation,' and the company is 'confident that increasing recognition in medical policy by commercial payers, the nearing profitability in APAC, and our leaner operating model set the foundations for an excellent FY27.' Management continues to caveat that if the current draft LCD is not finalised, Pacific Edge would need to undertake a significant restructuring and potentially raise further capital.

bull_case: The May 2026 draft LCD is the strongest positive reimbursement signal in the company's history - it explicitly names only Cxbladder Triage and Triage Plus as coverable, creating a potential de facto Medicare reimbursement moat versus all competing urine biomarkers if finalized as drafted

Triage Plus's approved draft price of US$1,328 (75% above the legacy US$760 price) materially improves unit economics and could flip the business toward profitability even without a big rebound in test volumes

Deep, purpose-built clinical evidence base (STRATA RCT, DRIVE study, AUA Grade A guideline inclusion, ongoing AUSSIE/microDRIVE/LOBSTER/CREDIBLE trials) gives Pacific Edge a multi-year evidentiary lead that would be very costly and slow for a competitor to replicate
Balance sheet has been meaningfully strengthened ($36.1m raised in May-June 2026) with management guiding to over 12 months of runway, reducing near-term insolvency risk while the LCD is finalized

Growing independent momentum outside Medicare - commercial payer wins (BCBS NC/SC/Kansas City, Highmark, Sentara covering a combined 12.5m+ lives) and APAC expansion (Singapore, Australia) diversify the revenue base and reduce single-payer dependency over time
bear_case: The LCD remains a draft, not final - Novitas retains full discretion on timing and content, and management itself states that if the current draft is not finalized including Triage/Triage Plus, the company would need a significant restructuring and likely more capital, with a real risk of investors losing some or all of their investment

Company has already diluted shareholders through at least three raises in roughly the past 12-14 months (August 2025 ~$20.7m; May 2026 $25.4m; June 2026 $10.7m) at depressed prices, and this pattern could recur if re-coverage slips further, especially given cash of only $7.8m at 31 March 2026 before the latest raise

US commercial infrastructure has been hollowed out (sales FTEs cut from 30+ to roughly 8-12) to conserve cash; even a positive final LCD will require re-investment and time to rebuild volume, meaning any recovery in revenue is likely to lag the coverage decision

FY26 net loss widened to $35.8m from $29.9m and revenue nearly halved (down 47.4%) even with the positive news arriving late in the year - the company has not yet demonstrated it can generate sustainable revenue growth or approach breakeven

Single-product, single-catalyst story - virtually all near-term equity value is tied to one binary regulatory outcome (the Novitas LCD) in one payer system (US Medicare), leaving the stock highly volatile and vulnerable to any adverse policy development, MAC contractor change, or delay
